Lindsay (Acme Health): Hey team — after the March 1st rerank rollout our search results are much worse. Previously citations and grounding were solid; now the model invents sources or returns unrelated docs. This started right after you said you pushed the reranker change. Example: query 'insulin dosing guidelines' used to return our clinical guideline doc; now it returns a third-party blog and misses the guideline we indexed.

maya_cs: Sorry to hear that, Lindsay. Sending this to eng + ML. Can you paste a minimal repro (query + API payload) and a couple examples of expected vs actual?

Lindsay (Acme Health): Yes — quick repro below. We call your retrieval+rerank endpoint from our production workspace. Payload: ```json
POST /v1/retrieve
{
  "workspace_id": "acme-health-prod",
  "query": "insulin dosing guidelines",
  "retriever": {"top_k": 100, "embedding_model": "embed-v2"},
  "reranker": {"model": "rerank-large-v2", "top_k": 10, "score_threshold": 0.45}
}```
Expected top result: "ACME Clinical - Insulin Dosing (2024)" with citation metadata id "doc:guideline-134". Actual top result: "HealthyLiving Blog - Insulin Tips" and the guideline doc rank drops to 12 with low reranker score (0.18).

sam_support: Noted. Did you see any change to embedding model or index rebuilds on your side?

Lindsay (Acme Health): No changes on our index. We haven't reindexed in weeks. The only change we observed was your March 1st note about updating the reranker model across prod.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-01T18:22Z — rollout: reranker-service v3.14 -> production (canary 10% -> 100%).

jun_ml: Thanks, this is likely a reranker/regression. A few quick asks: (1) can you share one full example with the doc ids (both expected and returned) and the raw reranker scores from your response? (2) do you have a short prompt/template you send to the reranker? (3) are you using any post-filtering (domain allowlist) currently?

Lindsay (Acme Health): Example response (sanitized): ```json
{
  "results": [
    {"doc_id": "doc:healthyblog-77", "rerank_score": 0.62, "source": "blog"},
    {"doc_id": "doc:paper-301", "rerank_score": 0.41, "source": "journal"},
    {"doc_id": "doc:guideline-134", "rerank_score": 0.18, "source": "internal"}
  ]
}```
We don't post-filter. Template to reranker is default (no custom prompt).

jun_ml: That makes it easier. Initial hypothesis: rerank model drift (v3 weights) changed relevance calibration for domain-specific clinical docs. We'll check model weights, calibration, and whether the scoring head or tokenization changed. Also check embedding/retriever alignment (embedding_model in payload is embed-v2; confirm that didn't change).

alex_sre: Also capturing this as page fault — low-latency but degraded quality. I'll pull the deploy timeline + canary metrics (error rates, request distribution) and any config flips.

maya_cs: Lindsay — I'll escalate and keep you updated hourly. Can you share two more queries where recall dropped (doc ids preferred)?

Lindsay (Acme Health): Sure — "pediatric insulin dosing" and "basal-bolus schedule for type 1". Both used to return internal protocols in top3, now absent.

jun_ml: Quick internal check: comparing rerank-large-v2 (previous) vs rerank-base-v3 (rolled out) on our eval set — I see a mean reciprocal rank (MRR) drop from 0.72 -> 0.54 on the clinical query slice. Also the calibration histogram shows more mass at low scores for internal docs. Could be a fine-tuning difference or a change in softmax temperature.

alex_sre: Canary traffic (10% window) showed a 2% positive delta in latency but nothing alarming. No spike in 5xx. Coverage of requests across workspaces matched expectations.

jun_ml: Can we get a raw side-by-side for Lindsay's exact query against both models? Sam, can you run the customer's payload through the staging endpoint pinned to rerank-large-v2 and then to prod reranker v3 and paste results? Use the customer's exact retriever params.

sam_support: On it. Running local repro. Will paste raw responses.```
# local commands
curl -X POST https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/retrieve -d '{"workspace_id":"acme-health-prod","query":"insulin dosing guidelines","retriever":{"top_k":100,"embedding_model":"embed-v2"},"reranker":{"model":"rerank-large-v2","top_k":10}}'```

sam_support: Staging (rerank-large-v2) result snippet: ```json
[ {"doc_id":"doc:guideline-134","rerank_score":0.78}, {"doc_id":"doc:healthyblog-77","rerank_score":0.43} ]```

sam_support: Prod (rerank-base-v3) result snippet: ```json
[ {"doc_id":"doc:healthyblog-77","rerank_score":0.65}, {"doc_id":"doc:guideline-134","rerank_score":0.18} ]```

jun_ml: That's a clear repro. Two potential immediate mitigations: (A) pin the customer to rerank-large-v2 for their workspace (config rollback) until we fix v3, (B) adjust score_threshold or expand retriever top_k to compensate. Option A is faster and safer.

alex_sre: I can push a workspace-level override to force reranker model for acme-health-prod. That will be a config change (no code deploy). Need signoff from PM/ops.

maya_cs: We should offer Lindsay option A (pin) and transparently explain rollback plan. Lindsay — would you like us to pin you back to the previous reranker while we investigate? :pray:

Lindsay (Acme Health): Yes please pin us back. This impacts patient-facing search so we need it rolled back ASAP.

alex_sre: I'll apply override now. Applying config: ```yaml
workspace_overrides:
  acme-health-prod:
    reranker.model: rerank-large-v2
```

deploy-bot: config change 2026-03-02T02:10Z — workspace override applied for acme-health-prod (reranker.model -> rerank-large-v2).

sam_support: Lindsay, can you confirm after ~2 minutes that results look like the staging output?

Lindsay (Acme Health): Confirmed — guideline doc is back in top1 with rerank_score 0.77. Huge relief, thank you.

jun_ml: Next steps for us internally: (1) open a regression ticket (ML-4532) to triage v3 differences, include repro cases and eval slice; (2) run ablation to see whether tokenization or training data causes the shift; (3) calibrate score scaling or add domain-specific fine-tune for clinical docs; (4) audit model rollout gating and add more domain slices to canary checks.

maya_cs: I'll keep this thread updated and follow up with a postmortem once ML team has root cause. Lindsay, apologies again and thank you for the quick repro — that's been super helpful.

Lindsay (Acme Health): Appreciate the quick response and the rollback. Please keep me in the loop on ML-4532.

jun_ml: Adding notes to ticket: reproduction examples attached, Canary metrics and MRR drop, quick rollback performed, suggestion to add a calibration shim or workspace pin API.

alex_sre: Closing the immediate P1 on our side since the override restored quality. We'll stay on call if needed.

maya_cs: Marking resolved for now; we will re-open if anything else crops up. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
